timeline.title: Thomas Markle Arrested on Child Sexual Abuse Material Charges
timeline.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been arrested in Florida on charges of possessing child sexual abuse materials. The Justice Department reported that the allegations include having sexually explicit photographs involving minors. Following his arrest, Markle appeared in court and is currently under house arrest after the FBI conducted searches of storage units he rented in the Los Angeles area.

event_overview.title: About Child Abuse
event_overview.subject: Child Abuse
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a federal criminal investigation and charge involving alleged possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) by Thomas Wayne Markle. It follows public reports of allegations involving material found among his possessions and an FBI investigation; the charge is an allegation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

facts.label: Charge and date
facts.value: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California announced on November 6, 2026 that Markle had been arrested on one federal count of possession of child pornography under 18 U.S.C. § 2252A(a)(5)(B).

facts.label: Jurisdiction and investigators
facts.value: The case was announced by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California, and the FBI is investigating; Markle’s initial appearance was expected in the Middle District of Florida because he was arrested in Florida.

facts.label: Alleged evidence location
facts.value: According to the Justice Department, FBI agents executed judicially authorized searches of two Los Angeles-area storage units registered to Markle and seized about 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books containing suspected CSAM.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: Section 2252A(a)(5)(B) prohibits knowingly possessing, or accessing with intent to view, material containing an image of child pornography when the required interstate-commerce connection is met; penalties for this subsection can reach 10 years, with higher maximums in specified circumstances.

facts.label: Terminology
facts.value: U.S. Justice Department guidance prefers the term “child sexual abuse material” because it describes the abuse and exploitation depicted, although federal statutes continue to use the term “child pornography.”

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the reported 2018-related police allegation and the November 2026 arrest; it does not establish guilt, provide a complete account of the investigation, or catalog all related reporting and court proceedings.
